name: One 97 Communications Ltd
title: One 97 Communications Ltd - 543396 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Paytm's Q1 FY27 call is a consumer and fintech growth story with no capacity or supply signals; management cites 8% EBITDA margin, 15-20% medium-term target, and cash build to ~INR 13,500 crore, with no hard numbers on UPI MDR.

guidance.value: 15-16% terminal margin cited by CEO; 15-20% range referenced
guidance.quote: it is 15-16% margin, so the direction is

guidance.value: 7.6 lakh; 25-30 lakh additions a year for lending
guidance.quote: we have said broadly 25 to 30 lakhs additions a year

red_flags.quote: in certain cases with merchants you are reducing your subscription rentals

evasions.quote: I don't have any clue of actually the number that it could be or not

summary.headline: Paytm Q1 FY27: management reports broad-based growth acceleration, with GMV up 31% YoY and EBITDA margin at about 8%, targeting a 15-20% medium-term margin.
summary.overview: Management said growth accelerated across all payment businesses, with GMV up 31% YoY (versus 23% in Q3 and 27% in Q4 as cited by an analyst) and sales and services revenue up 27% YoY. Adjusted for PIDF, the net payment margin moved from 8.4% to 8.8% (figures as discussed on the call), and management said the EBITDA margin is about 8% this quarter. Employee costs fell about 6.5% YoY excluding sales costs, which management attributed to AI-led efficiency and flat headcount rather than a one-off. Management framed the 15-20% margin as a medium-term direction, not a number to guide to, and said cash on the balance sheet was built up from INR 13,500 crore a year ago.

financial_highlights.change: Accelerated from about 27% in Q4 per analyst; management said acceleration is seen in every payments business
Adjusted for PIDF, growth of about 8% per management's commentary
Management cited a ~9 pp YoY improvement as discussed by an analyst
Rising gradually each quarter; analyst noted 10.6 to 11.2 bps increase in processing costs
Despite appraisals; management said no one-off and ESOP accounted for

financial_highlights.value: Management cited growth from INR 13,500 crore a year ago
financial_highlights.change: Balance sheet cash described as growing with strong free cash flow
Management expects roughly linear growth from here

segments.name: Payments (merchant / offline)
segments.commentary: Management said most profit comes from the merchant side, with growth accelerating; merchant loans are now a double-digit lending partner base. Management said offline is a strength.

segments.name: Consumer / P2P and UPI
segments.commentary: Management said P2P is not lower margin than P2M, and that monthly active users grew 8% YoY with GTV up 45%. Postpaid is still under INR 1,000 crore a month in usage.

segments.name: Financial services (lending, MTF, broking, MF distribution)
segments.commentary: Management said credit is distribution-led with no FLDG, partners' capital deployed is 4-6x Paytm's, and MTF is an ROI use of excess cash. Wealth/broking was described as a bright spot but still small.

segments.name: Marketing services
segments.commentary: Management said growth is behind merchant but not far behind, with travel as a headwind due to higher airfares and leisure demand.

guidance_outlook: Management did not give a numeric long-term EBITDA margin; directionally, it cited 15-16% as a terminal figure in one answer and 15-20% as the medium-term target.
Management expects 25-30 lakh lending additions a year, with the pace continuing.
Management expects continued profitability improvement, with investment in sales and marketing ongoing.
Management said the postpaid book could reach the INR 9,000 crore peak earlier, at about twice the earlier pace.
capex_capacity: Management said AI models were tuned in-house (a 4 billion parameter Indian-language model), running on Paytm's own infrastructure to cut compute costs.
No capacity or capex figures were given on the call.
demand_pricing: Management said GMV growth is broad-based across categories and not concentrated in a few businesses.
Management said Rupay credit on UPI continues to rise as a share of mix.
Management said fintech partners are seeing a desire to lend unsecured, with healthy bureau profiles.
Management said UPI MDR changes would have no material impact on Paytm, as merchants and enterprises paying or not paying MDR both benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins reach 20% long term, and what drives the margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not giving a number now and that margin is a trade-off with investment, but that the 15-20% range is structural. Drivers cited were operating leverage, AI-led efficiency and better unit economics.

qa_highlights.question: Is GMV acceleration sustainable and what is driving it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said acceleration is seen in every payments business, with offline and online growing at different rates. It said the growth is sustainable, with offline digitisation and the customer base as drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Will the government's UPI MDR change matter for Paytm?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has no visibility on the formula and is modelling it internally. It said there is no material impact, since merchants paying or not paying MDR benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Why are merchant subscription revenues being reduced on some plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this is a deliberate decision to discount subscription rentals for merchants with material revenue, to drive sign-ups, and that a tighter revenue recognition policy was applied on certain businesses.

qa_highlights.question: How much did employee costs fall, and is that sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no one-offs and that ESOPs are accounted for; minor quarter-on-quarter fluctuations are expected but nothing that changes the trend line.

qa_highlights.question: Is the lending industry's rapid growth a risk, and would APR cuts affect profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on the top-down industry figure. It said Paytm has launched lower-APR products and will lead on pricing if competitors enter.

risks_watch: Possible regulatory change to UPI MDR, which management said it is modelling internally.
Travel and leisure demand headwinds from higher airfares affecting marketing services revenue.
Industry-level digital lending growth and possible APR moderation or regulation.
Net payment margin pressure from processing costs and card mix (Postpaid interchange and card processing).
Consumer financial services trading volume headwinds that management said are only starting to turn.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth and AI efficiency, with management repeatedly signalling aggressive investment. It was evasive on numeric margin targets and on the UPI MDR question, citing uncertainty and no visibility.
key_quotes: The thing is that we probably announced 8% of EBITDA margin this quarter.
Cash is the spine and strength.
Currently we are tracking twice as fast as you expect.

growth.why: Q1 FY27 sales and services revenue reported up 27% YoY (about 8% adjusted for PIDF), with GMV up 31%; management gave no numeric revenue guidance and no capacity or capex figures, citing 25-30 lakh annual lending additions and a 15-20% medium-term margin direction (15-16% terminal) without a timeline.
